interpretation: The sequence model is the first input/architecture change in this track that beats the prequential tree on EVAL NLL with a CI excluding zero: N1 3-seed ensemble vs P -0.00361 [-0.00444, -0.00280] NLL and -0.00111 Brier; vs the recorded fit100 H0 the cumulative gain is -0.00539 (about 4x the recorded fit100-vs-OLD gain). The sequence encoder itself is responsible for -0.00232 (N1-N0, CI below zero; consistent per seed at -0.0015..-0.0019), while the plain MLP on the same features is only at parity with the tree per seed (N0-sk - P CIs cover zero) and gains from 3-seed averaging (-0.00129). Fair single-model reading: one N1 seed beats the single tree by -0.0012..-0.0015 NLL (all CIs below zero). The gain is largest for established pitchers (S3 -0.0043), i.e. the within-game sequence adds information the aggregate history profile lacks; for no-history pitchers (S0) and unseen batters (B0) the CIs cover zero. COST: top-label ECE gets WORSE for the neural arms (N1 ensemble vs P +0.0045 [+0.0005, +0.0061]; seed 2 alone +0.0105): the scalar temperature per head does not calibrate the neural logits as well as the tree's, so any fan-facing use needs a calibration pass (the E3 machinery, registered anew on these margins) before probabilities are shown. The ensemble-vs-single-tree comparison is not like-for-like; the per-seed numbers are the honest single-model effect. LIMITS: 2026 EXPOSED DEVELOPMENT, EVAL already exposed in scale-002/E1/E1b; CUDA runs are not bit-reproducible; 3 seeds; one architecture, no HPO; history pool 2026-only; research model, not the serving path; no adoption or winner claim. Suggested next: (1) calibrate N1 (vector/Dirichlet on its parent logits, registered) and re-check ECE; (2) prospective shadow logging of N1 ensemble predictions during the LCS/WS as a research shadow only, if the PM opens that work order.
